name: Lenko Digitigrade Street Low
description: A low-profile shoe built for the reverse-jointed digitigrade leg — the heel sits elevated on a sculpted platform that mimics natural hock positioning, with a deep toe box that tapers into a blunt, reinforced cap. Available in matte black, dusty olive, and a faded burgundy. The upper is soft synthetic canvas with reinforced stress points at the ankle joint where geneware legs apply unusual lateral force. Common on Tier 2-3 geneware adopters who got their leg mods done cheap and need shoes that actually fit without modification.
functionality: Ergonomic platform heel engineered for digitigrade gait mechanics. Reinforced lateral ankle support for non-standard joint stress.
what_it_says: You got the legs done, you're working with what you have, and you're not paying Spire prices to walk comfortably.
story_hooks: A pair found at a crime scene still has the original purchase receipt inside — from a shop that burned down six months ago.
Lenko's digitigrade lasts are rumored to be copied from a corponation patent, and a cease-and-desist might shut the brand overnight.
related_entities: Tessera Corponation ChronoMark VR-3 Passive Isotopic Citizen Tagging System

physical_description.visual_profile: A distinctly alien silhouette optimized for reverse-jointed digitigrade anatomy—the shoe appears to be pitched forward at an unnatural angle, with the heel platform elevated and the toe box extending downward in an almost bird-like configuration. The blunt, reinforced toe cap creates a squared-off profile that reads as deliberately engineered rather than organic. On a digitigrade wearer, the shoe aligns with the leg's biomechanics to create an eerily graceful stride.
physical_description.fit: Compression-hugging at the ankle joint with structured support at stress points; the elevated heel platform and tapered toe box are anatomically fitted to non-standard leg geometry. A standard human foot would find it completely unwearable.
physical_description.primary_material: Soft synthetic canvas upper with ballistic weave reinforcement at high-stress zones around the ankle joint and lateral stability panels.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly matte canvas with visible stitching and quilted reinforcement patches; the platform heel has a subtle grip texture.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary finishes in matte black (most common), dusty olive, and faded burgundy—all desaturated, worn-looking tones that suggest functional street gear rather than fresh retail.
physical_description.closures: Friction-fit with integrated ankle strap; no traditional laces or magnetic snaps—the shoe relies on geometric precision to stay seated on the digitigrade foot.
distinctive_features: Sculpted platform heel mimicking natural hock positioning
Deep, tapered toe box with reinforced blunt cap
Reinforced lateral ankle panels for geneware leg articulation stress
Visible stress-point stitching indicating budget manufacture
Slight wear/scuff patterns visible on toe cap and heel edge
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional: affordable geneware-compatible prosthetic footwear, accessible to working-class augmentation adopters.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals geneware adoption, street-level modification culture, and budget-conscious bodymods. Wearer is likely Tier 2-3 with visible augmentation and limited corporate polish.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in with minor scuffing; worn but maintained. Shows signs of street use without deterioration—a functional workhorse shoe.
